clue.text: Senior officer rushed round with relative suffering from drugs

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: the condition of someone drugged

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for rushed is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: rushed means ran
CO is a commanding officer
SIS is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A senior officer races about beside a relative who is under the influence of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the word for rushed backwards; the charade then starts with that turned word, not with the officer the clue names first.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is the medical term for a stupor or unconsciousness produced by drugs.

clue.text: Ample notice must be given before match

indicators.note: given before means the notice comes first, ahead of the match

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
to equate is to match one thing with another

explanation.surface: A rule that warning must be given ahead of a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient, which is the sense of ample here.

clue.text: Comedy consists of various raunchy tales

indicators.note: various means the letters come in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A comic play is made up of various bawdy stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Charley's Aunt is a Victorian farce by Brandon Thomas, a famous stage comedy.

clue.text: Miss rushes up, strict no end

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for rushes is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nip out is to rush or dash

indicators.note: no end means the last letter of the word for strict is dropped

parts.note: stern means strict

explanation.surface: A young woman hurries upstairs, strict to the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NIPS into SPIN; 'no end' cuts STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title for an unmarried woman, and a spinster is an unmarried woman.

clue.text: High-flier full of energy and very loud upset someone at work

indicators.note: full of means the high-flier holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a star is a high-flier

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read the other way

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
FF is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A high-achieving, energetic and noisy person upsets a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a star performer; 'upset' turns the energy and loudness letters upside down before 'full of' places them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A staffer is a member of staff, an employee at a workplace.

clue.text: How gin may be served cool

definitions.meaning: gin and It is gin mixed with Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A drinks tip: gin is best served chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is short for Italian vermouth, as in the British cocktail gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is a dated idiom for fashionable or up to date, which is to say cool.

clue.text: Vehicle in heavy demand on island

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a tax is a heavy demand on resources

explanation.surface: A vehicle that is much sought after on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Deadly accommodation didn't strike anyone as a joke

definitions.text: didn't strike anyone as a joke

parts.note: fell is an old word for deadly or ruthless, as in one fell swoop
a flat is accommodation, an apartment

explanation.surface: Grim lodgings that nobody found amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke that falls flat fails to get a laugh, an idiom for misfiring.

clue.text: Watercourse to suffer with minimal rain about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the words for minimal rain are placed around the other piece

parts.note: a trace of rain is the smallest measurable amount
to ail is to suffer or be unwell

explanation.surface: A stream that barely gets any rain is going to suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minimal rain' is a trace in the weather-report sense; 'about' wraps it round the word for suffer, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailrace is the channel carrying water away from a mill wheel or turbine.

clue.text: Very little say is given to a star

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, a little version of the word
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone with almost no voice is handed the role of a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' reads like 'scarcely any', but it is the shortened form of 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Ordinary freedom of factory worker to move around?

definitions.text: freedom of factory worker to move around?
definitions.meaning: read literally, the right of a mill hand to roam about the mill

explanation.surface: A question about whether a factory hand is allowed to wander about the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'run of' in its sense of free access, as in having the run of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-of-the-mill is an idiom for average or unexceptional, like goods straight from the mill.

clue.text: King with disorderly realm in truth? Reformer needed

indicators.note: disorderly means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.walkthrough: 'King with' is a nod: the reformer's name, with King added, is the US civil rights leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation in sixteenth-century Germany.

clue.text: Deplore feeble section of religious book

NT is the New Testament, a section of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone deplores a weak part of the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something is to mourn or express sorrow over it, synonymous with deploring it.

clue.text: Outside immutable, cross inside

indicators.note: inside means the cross symbol sits within the word for immutable

parts.note: eternal means unchanging, immutable
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places X in ETERNAL after the first E.

clue.text: This writer has a certain rhythm

indicators.note: has means the writer is followed by the other pieces, holding them after it

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves gives ME
certain means sure

explanation.surface: The setter claims to possess a definite sense of rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: In music and verse, a measure is a beat, metre or rhythmic unit.

clue.text: Maiden in accident almost quiet — lots of things seeming confused?

indicators.note: in means the maiden letter goes inside the shortened accident
almost means the last letter of the word for accident is dropped

parts.note: a mishap is an accident
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
SH is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A young woman in a near-accident, then silence, with everything looking muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final P of the accident word; 'in' sets the maiden letter inside what is left, near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble of many things.

clue.text: A part of body one gripped is most painful

indicators.note: gripped means held within, so the body part encloses the numeral

parts.note: the chest is part of the body
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A body part that someone has been gripping hurts more than anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one gripped' looks like a person being held, but 'gripped' places the Roman numeral inside the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Achiest is the superlative of achy, so it means aching the most.

clue.text: Carping officer briefly wanting admissions from those in debt

parts.note: Capt is the short form of captain, an officer

explanation.surface: A finicky officer is after written promises from debtors.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious means fault-finding, inclined to criticise petty points, just as carping is.

clue.text: Thus army chief traps deserter, employing a type of dialogue

indicators.note: traps means the chief's letters close around the deserter

explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' sets the deserter inside the Commander-in-Chief's initials, between the two Cs.

clue.text: Employees primarily work to feed fat cat

explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a large spotted wild cat.

clue.text: Put on fire — not the first time

indicators.note: not the first means the first occurrence of the letter is dropped

parts.note: to fire someone up is to stimulate them

explanation.definitionFit: To put on an accent or a show of feeling is to feign or simulate it.

clue.text: Shelter any number in a part of mansion?

clue.text: Keep watch on insects by river

clue.text: At which something becomes liquid in pot maybe?

clue.text: Son given mentor is someone trying hard

clue.text: Shame brought by Head of State in jibe against ethnic group
